The "Cliff Notes" version is... We (Americans) expect certain wages. Producing most consumer goods is a low-wage endeavor. Bringing production back to the US leads to an increase in price and lower sales.

We can force the issue with protectionist policy, but that doesn't change the underlying economic realities. Bringing production of cheap consumer goods back to the US would increase prices for everybody else.

In the long run, we are better off with free trade. We get the low prices we desire. The foreign country gets to develop an industrial base on which to build a large, prosperous economy. China over the last 20 years or so is a prime example - we get $1 t-shirts, they get factory jobs that increase their standard of living.

People want cheap goods, not high-quality goods.  Bringing production to the US at higher cost isn't going to change that.  Possibly the opposite; in an effort to maintain low prices, quality will slip.

Manufacturing in the US is UP over the past decade. 88% of manufacturing jobs lost have been lost to robots, not China.[1]
